findings.title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion when FGAP V2 is enabled
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). However, AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java, in the ClientRemovedEvent branch) calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on every client removal. When Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() now returns this ClientPermissionsV2, so deleting any client fires the event and the listener throws. Provider event listeners run synchronously inside the transaction, so the exception propagates and rolls back client deletion entirely. The V2 variant should either no-op here (V2 cleans up via orphan-resource removal) or the listener should skip clients for V2.

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token exchange whenever V2 feature is on
findings.body: canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) throws UnsupportedOperationException. The standard token exchange flow (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider) builds an evaluator via AdminPermissions.evaluator(session, realm, auth) and calls auth.clients().canExchangeTo(authenticatedClient, targetClient, token) for every client-to-client exchange, regardless of whether the realm uses fine-grained admin permissions. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns this class, so any token exchange to a different target client results in an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500) instead of an allow/deny decision. The unused getEvaluationContext helper and unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import suggest this method was left unfinished; at minimum it should fail closed with a proper denial rather than throwing.

findings.title: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles lack the manage fallback, denying role-based and manage-permission admins
findings.body: The three canMap* overrides only check hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). In V1 (ClientPermissions) these methods short-circuit with a manage check (manage-clients admin role / manage permission on the client), and the V2 Users implementation follows the same rule — testTransitiveUserPermissions in this PR asserts that a manage permission on users implies map-roles. Here, an administrator holding the manage-clients realm role or an FGAP manage permission on a client (or on all clients) gets canManage(client) == true but canMapRoles(client) == false, so role mapping for that client is denied. This is an access-control regression versus V1 and is inconsistent with the Users V2 semantics; the tests only pass because they grant the map-roles scopes explicitly.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can never return real client IDs
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission(scope) iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() to the result. However, per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) which never sets the resource type — only the type-level "Clients" resource created in init() has type set. So findByType never matches per-client resources (their type is null), meaning clients the caller was explicitly granted per-client permissions on are never returned. The only possible match is the "Clients" type resource itself, whose name is the literal string "Clients" — not a client ID — so the returned set is either empty or contains a bogus entry that callers comparing against client IDs (e.g., client listing filters) cannot use. The method effectively never returns a valid client ID.

findings.title: No migration for realms whose admin-permissions resource server was initialized with the Users-only schema
findings.body: init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, so realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change keep a resource server containing only the Users resource and the Users scopes. The new Clients scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) and the "Clients" type resource are never created for them. Consequences after upgrade: creating a Clients scope-permission fails validation in getScope with ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist."); creating a client resource in getOrCreateResource throws ModelException("No scopes found.") because the new scopes can't be found; and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to a null "Clients" resource. An upgrade/re-initialization path that adds the new scopes and the Clients type resource to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type, returning null display names
findings.body: getResourceName(session, policy, resource) only special-cases USERS resourceType (mapping to "All users" or the username). For a policy with resourceType "Clients" it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created via getOrCreateResource or init(), so the admin console/REST representation of client permissions shows blank resource names. It should mirror the Users handling (e.g., "All clients" for the type resource and the client's clientId for per-client resources).

findings.title: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) may call findByResource with a null resource
findings.body: In the fallback branch, resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) can return null (e.g., when the "Clients" type resource doesn't exist, or supportsAuthorizationSchema is false). The very next statement calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, which can throw a NullPointerException in store implementations that dereference the resource (e.g., resource.getId()) instead of simply denying access. A null check returning false should guard this call.

findings.title: Javadoc on requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() describes a boolean return for void methods
findings.body: The new javadoc for requireView() says "Returns true if canView() returns true" and requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true". Both methods are void and their contract is to throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* check fails (as correctly documented on the other require* methods). The documentation is misleading about the method contract and should say it throws ForbiddenException if the check returns false.
